newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank welcomes efforts to seek deal on assets.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank welcomes efforts to seek deal on assets.

text.p: The Bundesbank's policy-making council on Thursday welcomed efforts to resolve a dispute with Bonn over plans to revalue the central bank's assets, saying it hoped a compromise could be reached soon.

In a statement released after Thursday's regular policy meeting, the Bundesbank said: "The central bank council welcomed efforts to find a mutually acceptable resolution to these questions and the agreement on the central points reached in the talks held so far."

The Bundesbank two weeks ago shot down plans by Bonn to revalue the central bank's gold and currency reserves this year, aimed at creating an extraordinary profit which it planned to use to pay off old debt.

The Bundesbank raised two main objections -- that the plan interfered with the autonomy of the fiercely independent central bank, and that it would give Bonn extraordinary income in the key year for assessment of eligibility for entry to monetary union.

Bonn backed down on any revaluation for this year, and talks are now believed to concentrate on plans to revalue only currency reserves at the end of this year, creating the basis for a payout in 1998.

The central bank said its president Hans Tietmeyer and deputy president Johann Wilhelm Gaddum would continue to talk with Bonn over the issue. It added the central bank saw good prospects for a solution reflecting its stance.
